correctness.rationale: All positive polynomial factors increase on the nonnegative integers and the weight ratios tend to 1. Telescoping gives the degree-five norm-polynomial for W and P(0)/P(n) for its Cauchy dual. Laplace inversion of the two quadratics gives the difference of the damped sines with factor c^(-3)/(r^2-1); convolution with exp(-a u) adds the factor c^(-1) on rescaling. The resulting continuous-on-(0,1) signed density is integrable and unique by polynomial density, so a negative value at positive time is a genuine obstruction. Large damping makes the initial positive interval dominate the bounded later integrand; integration by parts makes the admissible set a closed upper ray. At zero separation and integer m the strict sine-multiple inequality off t=2 pi k gives precisely the quartic zeros. There the damping derivative is t_k/m^2 and the r derivative is zero. The trigonometric positivity inequality depends on the slow phase epsilon t exactly; replacing its rational coefficients by their resonant values incurs O(|epsilon|) uniformly at all times. The quartic versus |theta||phi| comparison yields log M_m(theta)=O(|theta|^(4/3)), so the positive variational maximum is attained. Above it, exponential slack dominates the uniform error for t beyond a fixed cutoff. Below the cutoff, short-time positivity and the O(|epsilon|^(4/3)) optimized loss near finitely many positive quartic contacts are controlled by the positive order-|epsilon| damping gain. Below the coefficient, times with prescribed fast phase and |epsilon|t approaching the selected slow phase give a strict negative witness, for both signs using evenness in theta. This proves the stated limit on the stipulated half-plane.
residual_risks: The observation about fixed tests concerns the leading critical separation: any fixed compact time range is positive for small nonzero detuning at each fixed positive K with delta=K|epsilon|, even below kappa_m. At delta=0 fixed positive resonance zeros can already reveal failure; this does not resolve the linear scale. Fixed truncated moment vectors at resonance are interior relative to normalization since the density is positive almost everywhere, and hence cannot distinguish this scale either.
No negative-separation, higher-order, or arbitrary-frequency classification follows from this proof.
